analysis.file_name: JPM _ US Energy_ Escalation Cocktail Hits Risk Assets, FY27 Strip New Highs, Russian Refinery Runs Rise, Global Runs Down 3.3mbd, EU Gas Supply & Demand, VLO, KMI, LBRT, KALU.pdf
analysis.title: JPM | US Energy: Escalation Cocktail Hits Risk Assets, FY27 Strip New Highs, Russian Refinery Runs Rise, Global Runs Down 3.3mbd, EU Gas Supply & Demand, VLO, KMI, LBRT, KALU
key_insights: Specialist sales desk (not Research) says global markets are trading risk off as oil volatility rises and early mega-cap earnings disappoint. It argues commodity conditions have deteriorated meaningfully in recent sessions.

Efforts to ease bottlenecks in freight and diesel have done little to stop price increases. Gulf attacks have grown in frequency and scope, and US and Israeli escalation increasingly looks like the base case.
Iran reports seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in the Strait overnight (unconfirmed). The market is already short freight, so tanker damage tightens it further.

Yesterday's attack on Shaybah (1mbd) is the latest sign that Saudi energy infrastructure is now in scope as it had not been earlier in the conflict. Operations were reportedly unaffected. The Houthi/Saudi conflict is splintering.
Embassy evacuations and Israeli fighter jet trials aimed at provoking Iran add to the case for abandoning de-escalation hopes. The 2027 WTI strip is pushing $88, a wartime high.

Counterweight: a WSJ article says Iranian oil on water has fallen from about 90mb to under 1 million since the US reimposed its blockade. Centcom says the blockade has denied Tehran about $25bn of oil revenue.

Vortexa estimates about 6 million barrels of Iranian oil sat off Singapore as of Oct. 9. Chinese refiners are turning to Brazil and West Africa, which the author sees as a structural threat to Iranian revenue even if the blockade is lifted. Oil is 30-40% of Iranian government revenue.

Russian crude processing rose to just over 3.7m b/d on Oct. 8-14, up about 50kbd from the first week of the month, as repaired plants offset lower runs at Omsk. Investors are skeptical about a ramp into year-end. Russia has said it could reach 3-3.5 metric tons of exports a month by year-end.
The API estimates global refineries are processing about 3.3mbd less than last year even after US and rest-of-world run increases, so the market needs the Russian runs.

EU gas: NWE+UK demand averaged 454 Mcm/day for Oct 12-18, up 13% WoW on colder weather, mostly in Germany. Month-to-date demand is 406 Mcm/day, about 20% lower YoY and 60 Mcm/day below JPM forecasts, driven by residential demand. October weather is about 0.2 stdev warmer than normal and the November outlook is 1.1 stdev warmer.
Asia LNG imports are on track for a three-month high in October despite spot prices at their highest in almost four years, per Kpler.

KMI beat on 3Q adj. EBITDA and raised its outlook, with the project backlog rising to $14.4bn. JPM expects a positive reaction but notes that 6-8% MTD outperformance versus WMB and DTM may limit the move and that investor feedback was mixed.

LBRT announced an agreement with an unnamed frontier AI lab for 1.2 GW of integrated power services. JPM expects a positive reaction, with a 500 MW ESA targeted by December 2026 and a significant capacity-fee prepayment in 4Q. Counterparty financial strength and contract length (CEO has messaged 15-year minimums) are the questions for the call.
KALU missed 3Q adj. EBITDA and guided FY26 EBITDA to the lower end of its range. FY26 FCF guidance was raised. JPM rates KALU Underweight.

VLO rose 2% pre-market on the 3Q print, which the desk calls slightly light. EPS beat versus Street was the smallest since 2Q24 and revenue was the first miss since 4Q23. Renewable Diesel segment was weak. Short positioning had already cleaned up into the print.
PCG fell 2% in pre-market as its data center pipeline grew only modestly after last quarter's 7.6GW increase. FY guidance was reaffirmed and the desk still views PCG as a held long versus EIX.
Reliance reported a strong 3Q beat and 4Q guide above Street on record shipments and pricing. JPM rates it Neutral.

Fortescue is in a price deadlock with CMRG, which has barred domestic mills from taking Super Special Fines (about 43% of FY26 shipments). Inventory is building at about 5Mt a month. JPM cut FY27 NPAT 15% but kept its $22 valuation and Overweight rating.
Crescent Energy (CRGY) agreed to buy DVN's Eagle Ford assets for about $3.85B, adding about 68 MBoe/d. JPM sees it lifting royalty cash flow by more than 25%.
Pre-earnings views: TC Energy is expected to beat and raise with 2027 guidance and Crossroads FID in focus. AltaGas is modeled above the high end of its 2026 EBITDA guidance.
Hudbay and Mitsubishi approved construction of the Copper World project in Arizona, with production starting in the back half of 2029.

Headline flow: US and Israel are reportedly drafting plans for resumed strikes on Iran after the midterms. IRGC says four oil vessels hit mines near Hormuz. Middle East oil exports are back near prewar levels per FT and Bloomberg. The US is releasing Northeast heating oil reserves.

market_movers.rationale: Spec first take calls the 3Q print slightly light versus a roughly $24 buyside EPS number and a $25 whisper. Revenue missed consensus by 3% and the Renewable Diesel segment was weak.
Beat and raise with the project backlog up to $14.4bn. JPM expects positive trading but flags that recent outperformance versus peers may cap the move.
1.2 GW power services agreement with a frontier AI lab and a 4Q capacity-fee prepayment. JPM expects a positive stock reaction.
3Q adj. EBITDA of $84M missed consensus by 13% on light shipments and margin pressure. FY26 EBITDA guided to the lower end of the prior range.
3Q adj EPS of $8.02 beat guidance by 23% and 4Q guidance beat Street by 30%, on share gains and price realization.
Quiet quarter with a smaller than expected data center pipeline increase. Guidance reaffirmed and the desk still sees it as a held long versus EIX.
JPM models 3Q26 adj EBITDA above Street and expects formal 2027 guidance supporting the high end of a 5-7% EBITDA CAGR.
Fortescue: FY27 NPAT cut 15% on lower achieved price assumptions and CMRG deadlock, valuation unchanged at $22 per share. Stock near a 5-year low.
Nickel Industries: EBITDA of $126m in line with JPMe. FY27 earnings estimate lowered by $12m and NPV down about 4%.

sector_views.rationale: KMI backlog growth and TRP's gas pipeline demand exposure are highlighted, with TRP described as peer-leading in growth visibility.
PCG data center pipeline growth slowed and PCG is still viewed as a held long versus EIX.

earnings_insights: KMI 3Q26 reported adj. EBITDA $2,180mm versus Street median $2,109mm and JPM estimate $2,025mm. Management sees 2026 EBITDA more than 6% above the $8.6bn budget, implying more than $9,114mm versus Street median $9,125mm. Backlog $14.4bn.

KALU 3Q reported adj EBITDA $84M versus pre-print consensus $97M, a 13% miss. FY26 EBITDA guided to the lower end of the +45-55% Y/Y range, implying about $450M and about $71M for 4Q. FY26 FCF guidance raised to more than $200M from $150-175M.

VLO 3Q reported (10/22): buyside EPS expectation about $24 ($23.65 average, $23.99 median) with a $25 whisper. EPS beat versus Street about 10%, the lowest since 2Q24. Revenue 3% below consensus. Renewable Diesel $353M versus STe $707.0M.

Reliance 3Q reported adj EPS $8.02 versus $6.40-6.60 guidance (+23%) and +18% versus pre-print Bloomberg consensus, including LIFO expense of $2.74/share versus $1.10 guided. 4Q guided to $7.40-7.60, 30% above pre-print consensus.
PCG 3Q: data center pipeline 12,870MW versus 12,710MW, 174MW energized versus 88MW in 2Q. FY guidance ranges of $1.64-1.66 and $1.78-1.82 reaffirmed.
LBRT 3Q26 results were described as mixed and overshadowed by the 1.2 GW frontier AI lab agreement. Capacity-fee prepayment expected in 4Q and initial 500 MW ESA targeted for December 2026.
TC Energy 3Q26 preview: JPM models adj EBITDA $2,928mm versus Street median $2,875mm and prior JPMe $2,720mm. These are estimates, not a print.

AltaGas 3Q26 preview: JPM models normalized EBITDA $340mm versus Street median $306mm and prior JPMe $287mm. JPMe 2026 EBITDA $2.16bn versus Street $2.10bn and guidance $2.0-2.1bn. These are estimates, not a print.
Nickel Industries 3Q26 reported EBITDA $126m, in line with JPMe.
Fortescue 1Q27 reported C1 costs of $22/t, $1.3/t below JPM forecast, and net debt of $2.8bn. FY27 guidance unchanged.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Weekly demand rose on colder weather, mostly in Germany, but month-to-date demand is 60 Mcm/day below JPM forecasts because of warm weather and lower residential use.

macro_indicators.reading: About 3.3mbd below last year per API estimate
macro_indicators.interpretation: Tight refined product supply keeps pressure on diesel and cracks, which is why rising Russian runs matter.

macro_indicators.reading: Just over 3.7m b/d, up about 50kbd from the first week of October
macro_indicators.interpretation: Recovery at attacked plants offset lower runs at Omsk. Investors doubt a ramp into year-end.

macro_indicators.reading: 23.31 million metric tons, a three-month high (Kpler estimate)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Asian buying continues despite spot prices at their highest in almost four years.

trade_ideas.rationale: Spec first take says PCG still feels like a held long versus EIX despite the quiet quarter.

risk_factors: Further escalation by the US and Israel against Iran and attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.
Damage to tankers in a freight market that is already short.
Skepticism that Russian refinery runs can ramp into year-end.
Fortescue CMRG price deadlock could force production cuts if unresolved by calendar year end.
LBRT has not formally signed its first ESA and counterparty strength and contract length are unknown.
KMI's recent outperformance versus peers may limit the reaction to its beat.
vol_and_positioning: KMI: investors may have tactically shorted ahead of the print after 6-8% MTD outperformance versus WMB and DTM, which JPM says may limit upside.
VLO: short positioning from late summer and early fall had cleaned up into the print.
Oil volatility is picking up and global markets are trading risk off per the desk.
geopolitical: Seven oil tankers reportedly caught fire or were damaged in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, per Iran (unconfirmed). Two more tankers struck as attacks spread across the Persian Gulf.
Attack on Saudi Shaybah field (1mbd) amid a splintering Houthi/Saudi conflict. Operations reportedly unaffected.
US blockade of Iran has cut Iranian oil on water from about 90mb to under 1 million and denied Tehran about $25bn of oil revenue per Centcom.
Embassy evacuations and Israeli fighter jet trials aimed at Iran. US and Israel reportedly drafting plans for resumed strikes on Iran after the midterm elections.
IRGC says four vessels carrying oil hit mines near Hormuz and warns the US of wider responses.
Conflict in the Middle East began February 28 when the US and Israel attacked Iran.
Russia says it will send its first diesel cargo to the US on Thursday. Ukraine attacks on Russian refineries have cut and then restored runs.
US sanctions on a Greece- and Panama-based law firm over aid to Iranian shipping.

tension_points.bull_case: Bull case for oil prices: attacks on tankers and Saudi infrastructure are rising in cadence and scope, escalation is the base case and the 2027 WTI strip is at a wartime high.
tension_points.bear_case: The US blockade has cut Iranian oil on water to under 1 million barrels and denied about $25bn of revenue, and Chinese buyers are shifting to Brazil and West Africa, which could pressure Iran's ability to finance the conflict.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The author notes the argument weakens if the blockade is removed, since much of the lost revenue would return.

tension_points.bull_case: Sanctioned projects exceeded expectations, the backlog rose to $14.4bn and JPM expects positive trading.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors may have shorted into the print after 6-8% MTD outperformance versus peers, and bears focus on the next catalysts, including the flatter 2027 EBITDA budget due in early December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM sees the December 2027 EBITDA budget as already well understood, so a surprise there would undercut its view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Attacks in the Gulf have risen in cadence and scope and escalation increasingly looks like the base case.
theme_stances.evidence: escalation by the US & Israel, increasingly appears to be the base case

theme_stances.key_argument: Collapse in Iranian floating storage and loss of Chinese customers threatens Tehran's revenue on a structural basis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Global refining runs remain well below last year, so recovering Russian runs are needed.
theme_stances.evidence: We’re going to need those runs.
